Kill the Great Olm in a solo raid without taking damage from any of the following: Teleport portals, Fire Walls, Healing pools, Crystal Bombs, Crystal Burst or Prayer Orbs. You also cannot let his claws regenerate or take damage from the same acid pool back to back.
column10: Olm starts off each phase beginning with two auto-attacks before performing its first special attack, Crystal Burst. | The most dangerous threat for this achievement are the fire walls and teleport portals; if the player is on the Arceuus spellbook, they won't have any ideal means of dispelling the fire walls apart from carrying a water source (e.g watering cans) on them. | Teleport portals can also have a range of 10 tiles from the player, which when focused on Olm may make them hard to spot in time. | In order to successfully pull off the achievement, the player must utilise the safespots as shown by the picture to the right. | These spots will always force the head to turn accordingly based on its location: | Spots 1 and 8 always force the head to turn right. | Spots 4 and 5 always force the head to turn left. | When running from spot 4, running to spot 2 will ensure the head turns right as long as the right hand has been damaged. | If the right hand is not damaged, it will turn to the middle. | Due to this, the player can then run from spot 2 to spot 3 to land an additional attack and force Olm's head to the middle after it turns right. | The same also applies when running from spot 5 to 7. | Running from spot 1 to spot 3 forces the head to turn to the middle. | The same also applies when running from spot 8 to 6. | When Olm is forced to turn his head around to find the player, he will skip an attack in the process. | However this shouldn't be much of an issue with a smooth run. | A proper 4:1 (with a 4-tick weapon) or 3:1 (with a 5-tick weapon) should avoid all attacks outside of the flame walls and acid pools for the melee hand. | The magic hand can still be dealt with using normal methods. | Crystal bombs should not be an issue unless one is within proximity of the running tiles. | If the player wants to take no chances, the much slower 1:0 method (with any weapon) may be used, as this guarantees Olm will never be able to attack the player. | During phase 4, the teleport attack and crystal bombs are no longer used, but the flame wall and acid pools will still persist. | A player can still safely attack Olm with ranged using a crossbow or twisted bow without fear of retaliation by the head. | The falling crystals during this phase will not disqualify players from the achievement, though they can prove to be a problem if low on supplies. | Dying to Olm will not disqualify players from the task, as long as they died to a standard attack.

column6: Kill the Great Olm in a trio raid without any team member taking damage from any of the following: Teleport portals, Fire Walls, Healing pools, Crystal Bombs, Crystal Burst or Prayer Orbs. You also cannot let his claws regenerate or take damage from the same acid pool back to back.
column10: Solo: Follow the Perfect solo Olm strategy. | As the task only requires Olm to be killed this way in a trio raid, one or two players can still handle the task, although extra time is likely to be needed due to the scaled stats. | Since the task doesn't disqualify players who die to Olm's standard attacks, players can suicide supplies if necessary. | Trio: If you want to do it as an actual trio, keep the following in mind: | - Lightning special attack hitting you does not fail the achievement. | Still avoid it whenever you can since you might get stuck in a poison pool or flame wall. | - The every-other-tick falling crystal attack that can occur during crystal phase does not fail the achievement if it hits you. | Tank the hits in order to ensure you do portal special successfully. | - Poison trails are the most likely thing to fail the achievement. | Whenever Olm looks at you during acid phase and head phase, start walking and do not attack until he turns away. | If you get the acid trail on you, just keep walking until it is gone. | - In order to minimise specials during phase 3, it is beneficial to directly set the head as you normally would during phase 1 and 2, and have the runner hybrid down the melee hand. | Hail Mary: If you do happen to get the portal special and acid trails at the same time, have the person with an acid trail walk from one side of the room to the other (ctrl-click). | The other person can get a few tiles ahead and try to ctrl-click in the same direction at the proper tick. | If you take poison damage, turn on run for one tick and then turn it off again.

column6: Kill Tekton without taking any damage.
column10: You do not need to receive kill credit for Tekton in order to complete this achievement. | So it is easiest to get a partner to tank him and do most of the damage while you land one damaging hit. | In order to speed up the kill you can have the partner stand on the opposite side of Tekton and hit him only right after he swings at your partner then walk away like you would at guardians. | Lure Tekton to the centre of the arena, away from any pillars of smoke, as these have erratic hitboxes and can deal 1-3 damage when standing on them, disqualifying them from the achievement. | Use one of the flinching or running methods to avoid Tekton's standard attacks. | Be careful of the fireballs launched during his repair state as they have a 3x3 AoE; while they should generally hit together, they may occasionally desync and hit on different ticks due to travel distance. | Unlike other cox combat achievements, you need to be in the room at the end of the fight to complete the achievement. | Entering through Tekton's fire will fail the achievement, meaning the player must be present the whole fight. | For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.

column10: For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health. | By having another player use protect from range and dodge the demon's attacks in the centre of the room, additional players can stand on the north/eastern walls and avoid the demon's aggression completely. | Using Fire Surge will help secure kill-credit over players using ranged. | Ironmen must be the only player damaging the Ice Demon to complete this combat achievement.

Complete a Chambers of Xeric (Solo) in less than 21 minutes.
column10: Look for a raid with extremely easy and simple rooms, if possible, try to align this with the grandmaster variant. | There is a 4 minute gap between this and the grandmaster variant, though taking either master or grandmaster variants are acceptable for this achievement. | Ideal layouts for a raid can include: | Vasa, Vespula, Tekton, Tightrope, Crabs | Vasa, Vespula, Tekton, Crabs, Guardians | Vanguards, Tekton, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs | Vasa is a very fast room when a twisted bow is used alongside a dragon warhammer, assuming that the hammer does land at least once in the fight. | Vespula can be easily taken out by using either the twisted bow or a Tumeken's shadow. | Tekton can be easily dealt with using Osmumten's fang if no Scythe of Vitur or Inquisitor's mace is available. | Tightrope can be skipped if needed and crabs are fairly straightforward to do, assuming the ideal layout. | This will result in 4 brews, 2 restores, prayer enhances and overloads, which is more than enough for an experienced player at Olm. | Vanguards are only put on the list as it is possible to clear them fast with good gear. | Vanguards can provide 3-6 brews, 0-3 restores and 1 overload, which is even more supplies, but they do take longer to kill compared to the other rooms. | Muttadiles can provide a full set of one brew, restore, prayer enhance and overload, however, due to the high variance in each fight this room can consume a lot of supplies if unlucky and thus discouraged from attempting this room for the sake of time.

column6: Complete a Chambers of Xeric (Solo) in less than 17 minutes.
column10: Pick a raid with very fast to clear rooms while minimising supply usage, as the player is expected to no-prep Olm. | Layouts with fast rooms, at least 1 overload and some supplies are ideal. | 3 combats and 2 puzzles is the smallest possible layout, Tightrope and crabs are the fastest puzzle rooms allowing 3 combat rooms for the other supplies. | Commonly wanted combat rooms are: Vasa (2 Xeric's aid+ and an Overload+) and Vespula (2 Xeric's aid+, Revitalisation+, Prayer enhance+ and an Overload+). | Tekton and Muttadile (Need to freeze both muttadiles) can still be used but are usually slower and are substituted for Shamans since the changes that allows Vasa and Vespula to drop overloads. | A (Vasa, Tekton, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs) layout will provide the player with four brews, two restores, prayer enhances and overload, which should be more than enough for the player to use at Olm. | A (Vasa, Shamans, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs) is a slightly faster layout but results in 1 less restore. | Make sure to make the most of your inventory to fit all the supplies, since it is more important to finish the raid than trying to organise in the chest. | Tightrope skipping is highly encouraged to save additional time, as it significantly cuts the room's completion time and uses minimal supplies. | Tightrope can be substituted for guardians if possible, which saves some supplies but will result in a slightly slower room. | The player should initiate the fight with Olm before 7 minutes as the half of the time needed completing this achievement will come from fighting Olm. | Using thralls are highly recommended to deal additional damage.

column10: The easiest way to obtain this achievement is to kill Zalcano solo, not using any imbued tephra on Zalcano but instead waiting for the golem to spawn and using your imbued tephra on the golem. | The most reliable way to complete this achievement is to attack golems when standing on a blue circle, in order to maximise damage. | If there are no blue circles when the golem spawns, try to attack it as soon as possible, so that it's possible to fire multiple tephra at it. | Without the blue circle damage boost, it will likely take several tephra to kill a golem.

column10: The easiest way to complete the combat achievement is to use the Scorching bow, as its special attack always freezes K'ril in place. | With sufficient damage, K'ril can be killed without him being able to attack the player at all, guaranteeing the combat achievement. | Alternatively, players can use a kiting method to stay out of melee range. | K'ril only uses his special attack against players using Protect from Melee. | Therefore, a good strategy that uses melee only is to instead use Protect from Magic along with strong melee armour; a super combat potion and Emberlight or Arclight are also recommended.

column6: Finish off K'ril Tsutsaroth whilst all of his bodyguards are dead.
column10: A good method to complete this task solo (and the similar tasks for each of the respective God Wars Dungeon bosses) is to use a Toxic blowpipe alongside a Serpentine helm to envenom the bodyguards between kills, which will put the minions at near-death by the time the boss is nearly dead.

column6: Defeat K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance using only demonbane spells.
column10: Recoil damage (i.e. ring of recoil, echo boots, or Vengeance), Undead Grasp, as well as thralls, will disqualify players from completing this achievement. | Additionally, ironmen instances do not work; players must use private instances for this achievement. | While demonbane spells are effective against most demons, K'ril's magic defences still makes them fairly inaccurate, mandating players to also cast Mark of Darkness to increase their accuracy and damage further. | A purging staff will further double their bonuses, though the staff of the dead or toxic staff of the dead are viable alternatives as they too can autocast demonbane spells, and have a special attack that reduces all melee damage by 50% for one minute. | Lastly, a slayer helmet (i) may be worn while on a greater demon slayer task to further increase accuracy. | Players can also cast Ward of Arceuus to reduce damage taken by 10%. | Most normal supplies can be forgone as this strategy is only to stay for the one kill needed for the combat achievement. | A cheap form of antipoison, such as an araxyte venom sac | 2-3 super restores or Sanfew serums if not bringing another form of antipoison | Runes to cast Dark Demonbane, Mark of Darkness, and Ward of Arceuus | Stat boosts such as an Imbued heart and Super defence | Ghommal's hilt 1 or better to get there | Any teleport to leave

column6: Kill K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance without taking any of his melee hits.
column10: This can be achieved with the use of Protect from Melee and a bit of luck. | K'ril Tsutsaroth has a 1/9 chance to use his 'prayer smash' special attack when praying against his melee attacks, which cannot be avoided and will fail the challenge. | Maximising your damage output with the use of weapons such as Arclight and special attack weapons such as dragon claws is recommended to minimise the chance he can perform the attack before dying. | Ironman instances do not work, meaning that ironmen have to use the private instance to complete this task. | Another strategy is to walk under K'ril Tsutsaroth until his health bar disappears, and attacking him once before walking back under him again. | If you can succesfully stand under him after every attack, he will never be able to hit you. | Switching your NPC attack options to 'always right-click' will make this easier to do. | Slower weapons with higher strength bonuses such as the elder maul, godswords and the crystal halberd can be very useful as their low attack speed does not matter when using this method, while they can hit very high on each attack. | Other flinching methods that K'ril doesn't hit at all (6:0, 8:0, 9:0, etc) are also viable options for this achievement and requires no luck if the method is done perfectly.

column6: Kill K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance without ever being hit by his bodyguards.
column10: A simple method to achieve this is to use the 5:0 method with a powerful weapon such as Tumeken's shadow, while replacing some damage-boosting gear (e.g., ancestral robe top, tormented bracelet, magus ring) with tank gear (e.g., blessed d'hide body/justiciar chestguard, barrows gloves, ring of suffering (ri)) for the ranged or mage minion not being prayed against. | The damage output should still be high enough to kill K'ril in a few cycles, while offering enough defence to block most of the minions' attacks. | An additional benefit of this strategy is that it can be used in a regular extended trip, saving the costs of repeatedly creating private instances for each attempt. | It is also possible to complete this challenge by prayer flicking the minions perfectly. | To offset the attacks, start under either the mage minion or ranged minion, so it will attack one tick later than the other, and by kiting the melee minion while flicking the ranged and mage minion; alternatively, the player may start a fresh kill towards the east side of the arena, resulting in the ranged minion moving into attack range later. | Another option is to focus on killing K'ril Tsutsaroth as quickly as possible using special attack weapons such as dragon claws without prayer flicking; however, as dumping special attacks alone will not be enough to kill K'ril, the player should bring tanky gear to finish K'ril off safely while under attack from the minions. | One last option is to keep either the mage or ranged alive and at low health between kills until just after K'ril Tsutsaroth spawns. | Immediately kill the minion once the boss spawns and pray against the other minion as you defeat the boss.

column6: Finish off K'ril Tsutsaroth with a demonbane weapon.
column10: Killing him with demonbane spells will count towards completion, even without a Purging staff. | Kril's health can be lowered with another weapon, but the final blow must be done with a demonbane weapon. | Darklight, or its upgraded form, Arclight, are the most readily available for most players.

column6: Kill K'ril Tsutsaroth 20 times in a private instance without leaving the room.
column10: As K'ril and his bodyguards drop ashes and not bones, the player's healing will primarily come from using Blood Barrage on stacked Tstanon Karlak and Zakl'n Gritch after each kill. | The bodyguards can supplement (though not replace) healing with Sharks or Tuna Potatoes drops. | Due to K'ril's high and unpredictable damage, learning a kiting method (such as the 5:0 twisted bow/tumeken's shadow or the 8/9:0 Bow of Faerdhinen/scorching bow methods) is strongly recommended for this achievement. | The scorching bow has the added benefit of binding K'ril with its special attack, with enough DPS to kill him within two specials, which allows for some much easier kills. | A Lightbearer and Death Charge can regenerate further special attack for these easier kills (though Death Charge use conflicts with Blood spells, and should only be brought if the player is comfortable flicking the minions instead). | The shared instance for ironmen does not count for this achievement.

column6: Kill a Jal-Zek within the Inferno.
Complete the Inferno 5 times.
Kill Tzkal-Zuk without letting Jal-ImKot dig during any wave in the Inferno.
column10: A Jal-ImKot will burrow towards the player if they have not been able to attack them for 50 ticks after the start of a wave. | Letting it attack you at any point instantly resets its dig-timer, and allows you more options than a DPS race to kill the enemy immediately after the start of the wave. | A simple approach for this task is to complete it alongside the Budget Setup grandmaster task, utilising a longer ranged weapon, such as the bow of Faerdhinen and full crystal armour, or Eye of Ayak or Tumeken's shadow with mage armour, as it is typically failed when Jal-ImKots spawn further south and cannot easily be reached with the toxic blowpipe. | Otherwise, it is important to be comfortable quickly off ticking common stacks to run within range of the Jal-ImKot soon after the start of the wave to blowpipe it down before it can dig, or letting it attack you so you gain additional time before it digs.

column6: Complete wave 68 of the Inferno within 30 seconds of the first JalTok-Jad dying.
column10: Since healers spawn when a Jad reaches half health, it is recommended to trigger the spawn of healers for each Jad before killing the first one. | Kill or trap each set of healers as they spawn. | After all three Jads have spawned healers and their healers have been dealt with, lower each Jad's health carefully, ensuring not to kill any prematurely. | Once each Jad is sufficiently weakened, swiftly kill each Jad in succession.

column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without being attacked by TzKal-Zuk and without taking damage from a JalTok-Jad.
column10: Jads will appear on waves 67-69. | One Jad will appear on wave 67 and should prove to be no problem. | Three Jads will appear on wave 68 with an attack speed of 9 instead of 8 and attack in a staggered rotation to allow players to pray against all three. | While fighting Zuk, players must be behind the Ancestral Glyph before he attacks, as it will block the incoming attack meant for the player. | Therefore, if his attack goes for the player instead, the achievement is voided. | In addition, a final Jad will appear during the fight when Zuk reaches 480 health for the first time.

column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without letting a pillar fall before wave 67.
Kill Tzkal-Zuk without letting your hitpoints fall below 50 during any wave in the Inferno.
column10: All waves will need to be dealt with cautiously, as all of the Inferno monsters hit very hard and the later waves will consist of multiple monsters that use different combat styles, which can easily combo the player out if their attacks aren't protected against. | The primary threats for this achievement generally involve double Jal-Aks, a Jal-Zek with a Jal-Xil, or any combination of the three monsters. | Try to heal to full (and overheal if necessary) before the start of the next wave to minimise the chance of falling below 50 hitpoints. | Once the first Jal-Zek appears, players are highly encouraged to have Protect from Magic on before the start of the next wave, as the mager has a max hit of 70, which will drop the player below the threshold if they aren't fully boosted (120 or 121 hitpoints). | The other monsters have lower max hits, with the ranger having a max hit of 46. | Jal-ImKots have a max hit of 49, but they can only attack in melee distance. | In these waves with magers, players can position the monsters and use justiciar armour and Protect from Magic to maximise ranged defence. | During Zuk's wave, the damage is more predictably avoided. | When Zuk summons his Jal-MejJaks, their blasts will not void the achievement if they drop the player's health below 50, since it isn't a targeted attack. | However, if any other monster attacks them off prayer while their health is below 50, they will void the achievement.

column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without equipping a Twisted Bow within the Inferno.
column10: Effective alternative ranged weapons to the twisted bow include the bow of Faerdhinen or Zaryte crossbow along with a toxic blowpipe. | Using a Tumeken's shadow (optionally with an Eye of Ayak) is also viable, although care must be taken due to the lower defences of magic armour.

column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without using any magic spells during any wave in the Inferno.
column10: Blood Barrage can no longer be used as a means to restore health, so alternate means of healing include the Saradomin godsword (also restores prayer), ancient godsword (less efficient) or toxic blowpipe. | Chinchompas or a venator bow will be needed to kill the Jal-Nibs. | While the achievement's description states that all spells cannot be used, there are some exceptions. | For example, summoning thralls and Death Charge will not cause the achievement to be failed. | Similarly, the eldritch Nightmare staff special attack does not fail the task despite it being a targeted attack and calculating damage based on magic level and magic strength.

column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without equipping any range or mage weapons before wave 69.
column10: Justiciar armour and Dinh's bulwark are recommended for the massive ranged defence bonus and passive damage reduction effect, reducing a good chunk of damage from the ranged mobs during the run. | A Saradomin godsword is recommended to restore health and prayer points. | Even then, try to get as few enemies as possible attacking to avoid the chances of getting combo'd out, since all of the monsters can hit very hard. | The player is still allowed to cast spells as long as they don't equip a wand or staff; as melee armour provides negative magic bonuses, they will need to be taken off in order for the spells to hit. | Alternatively, a Voidwaker and Ancestral robe top likely provides enough positive magic accuracy to allow barrage spells to hit. | Note that despite polestaves such as the pharaoh's sceptre and keris partisan being unable to autocast spells, they are still considered magic weapons and will fail the task if equipped. | It is highly recommended to bring both a noxious halberd and scythe of Vitur for this task if the player can manage the monsters. | The halberd is very useful for players who don't want to flinch monsters without running the risk of other monsters attacking or getting melee'd by a ranger, mager, or Jad. | This is especially true in the triple Jad wave, as letting one use melee will cause the Jads to potentially attack in sync when the player already has to focus on flicking incoming attacks. | DO NOT equip a magic or ranged weapon after clearing the triple Jad wave; wait for Zuk's cutscene to start before doing so. | If the weapon is swapped to before Zuk's wave starts, the attempt will be void.

column5: Jad? What Are You Doing Here?
column6: Kill Tzkal-Zuk without killing the JalTok-Jad which spawns during wave 69.
column10: JalTok-Jad will appear during Zuk's fight when he reaches 480 or lower hitpoints. | As the task requires players to not kill this particular Jad, players will need to watch Jad's animations while moving alongside the Ancestral Glyph to avoid getting killed by Jad. | It is beneficial, although not completely required, to know when the Jal-Xil and Jal-Zek will spawn, as to minimise distractions as it is possible for them to attack in sync with each other.

Subdue Tempoross, getting rewarded with 10 reward permits from a single Tempoross fight.

column10: This can be achieved by loading both cannons of one ship, then travelling across Tempoross Cove to load the cannons of the other ship. | The four cannons do not need to fire simultaneously. | If attempted during the whirlpool phase, the player will be able to run between ships without the risk of being caught in a wave.

column6: Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's second challenge.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fourth challenge.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's sixth challenge.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's first challenge in less than 45 seconds.
column10: An easy way to complete this challenge is to use full Dharok's, a Defence-lowering special attack weapon (elder maul, dragon warhammer, or Bandos godsword), Dinh's bulwark (optional), and Vengeance. | Additionally, bring several anglerfish (you will need one for each attempt), super combat potions, and a locator orb. | If you don't have a Dinh's bulwark, you can alternatively use chinchompas, darts or throwing knives to get the healers' aggression, which additionally has the benefit of being able to use two Defence-lowering special attacks per attempt, or bringing a DPS spec weapon such as Dragon claws. | Before you enter the challenge, equip the special attack weapon, cast Vengeance, drink a super combat potion, and eat an anglerfish. | After you enter the challenge, activate Piety and activate your Defence-lowering special attack. | When Jad spawns, instantly attack him. | If the special attack does not land and/or Jad hits less than 80 damage, die or exit the challenge and try again. | If the special attack lands and Jad hits high, activate Protect from Melee and switch to Dharok's greataxe. | Lower your hitpoints to below 10 with the locator orb. | If Jad attacks with magic or ranged, try changing your prayer as late as possible, especially if the healers are also attacking you. | It should take at most 2-3 hits to spawn the healers. | When they spawn, immediately lure them with darts, knives, or the Dinh's bulwark special attack. | Switch back to your greataxe and finish off Jad.

column6: Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's third challenge in less than 3 minutes.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fifth challenge in less than 5 minutes.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's second challenge with only melee.
column10: JalTok-Jad's melee attack speed is faster than its Ranged and Magic attacks. | Melee attacks will alter the cycles with the other Jad making protection Prayer switches between two Jads much more difficult. | To avoid this, a halberd is highly recommended as it will allow players to maintain the necessary distance to prevent the Jads from attacking in sync with each other. | The noxious halberd is the strongest choice due to its higher stats and faster attack speed over the crystal halberd. | This is only needed for the first Jad, as the other Jad is less of an issue. | There is no restriction on manually casting magic spells, but a magic weapon cannot be equipped at any point during the fight. | Using any dagger which has a +1 magic bonus, will not fail the challenge if used to manually cast spells while equipped; however a Pharaoh's sceptre or Keris partisan will, despite also not having autocast options. | This can be useful for barraging the Yt-HurKots to grab their attention, as running out from the centre may result in the Jads attacking in sync.

column6: Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fourth challenge with only melee.
column10: JalTok-Jad can attack with melee every , as opposed to its normal attack speed when using Ranged or Magic attacks. | Melee attacks will alter the cycles with the other Jads making protection prayer switches between four Jads much more difficult. | To avoid this and melee attacks from the first three JalTok-Jads, a halberd can be used to attack with melee from a distance. | The last Jad can be killed with any melee weapon while praying protect from melee and switching when necessary. | To lure the healers effectively, it is possible to use the special attack of Dinh's bulwark, which can hit all the healers in one attack. | Because healers don't spawn on a Jad's east side, prepare for your spec by standing on the west side. | You can use any type of thralls for this Combat Achievement.

column6: Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's third challenge without having anything in your inventory.
column10: Using a twisted bow or even a bow of Faerdhinen (with full crystal armour) makes this challenge quite easy. | Only attempt with a magic set-up if you own a Tumeken's shadow. | Other set-ups will significantly increase kill times. | You can pre-pot/eat prior to entering the challenge. | It is recommended to use the ancient mace special attack in your POH with max melee gear, eat an anglerfish, and drink a dose of prayer regeneration potion prior to entering. | With both 99 Prayer and Hitpoints, this will allow you to enter with 121 HP and up to 142 prayer points depending on gear available, plus an additional 1 prayer point restored every 12 ticks up to a maximum of an additional 66 prayer points. | It is advised to also sip a combat style appropriate potion prior to entering. | Only use protection prayers without using any stat boosting prayers such as Rigour. | At 99 prayer points, a +15 prayer bonus will allow you 445 seconds (7:24) of prayer during the challenge. | At 139 prayer points and +20 prayer bonus, using just protection prayers will last over 11 full minutes allowing you to easily complete the challenge. | If you are running out of prayer before you can kill all three, prioritise increasing prayer bonus over slight DPS increases, such as a ring of the gods (i) rather than a venator ring for an additional 8 prayer bonus. | A good strategy for healers is to tag each one, and try running through JalTok-Jad to block them on the opposite side. | Good equipment can allow you to tank some of the healers, but it is not advised, as even one healer from each Jad is enough to kill you. | To time your run-through, stand just outside Jad's melee range, and as the attack animation starts run through, praying accordingly. | This allows you to take almost no damage from the healers.

column6: Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fifth and sixth challenges back to back without failing.
Complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's third challenge while using a different attack style for each JalTok-Jad.
column10: Since JalTok-Jads are very resistant to magic, it is advisable to start with ranged. | Because Jad's melee attacks are faster than the ranged and magic attacks, killing the second one with magic is advisable, as using melee will likely offset the attack cycles of the two remaining Jads or even synchronize them. | Kill the last one with melee, and the challenge is complete. | Recoil damage from a ring of suffering (r) or echo boots along with the sacrifice damage from ancient godsword special attack will cause you to fail this combat achievement. | Thralls can be used, but the style of thrall summoned must match the attack style used to kill each Jad, or you will fail this combat achievement. | Therefore, after killing a Jad, it is advised to summon a thrall of the next combat style as you switch your gear.

column6: Defeat the Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode without letting blood spawns create more than 15 blood trails.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;The Maiden of Sugadinti;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode;blood spawn
column10: Blood spawns can appear at random during the fight against the Maiden, but their chances of appearing significantly increase if the Maiden's splatter attack manages to hit someone; thus, any melee users should carefully watch the Maiden's animations, as they will have less time to react compared to those attacking from afar. | As the Maiden is generally killed with melee (as it is significantly higher damage when her Defence level is drained), players should be careful. | If a blood spawn appears, the mager is responsible for freezing it in place; as they have near non-existent stats, there should be no issue of splashing in mage gear. | An Ice ancient sceptre can be useful for the task, as it will bind the spawn for 21.6 seconds when using Ice Barrage compared to 19.2 seconds. | An alternate strategy takes advantage of the fact that blood spawns that spawn in the north-east corner of the arena cannot move. | To take advantage of this, a player can enter, stand on the north-east corner of the area until a blood splat attack occurs, then intentionally step on it to spawn a blood spawn. | Then finish the rest of the kill without stepping on another blood splat.

column6: Defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode with at least 3 people in the room, without anyone in your team standing on top of each other.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Pestilent Bloat;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode
column10: Being able to damage the bloat quickly is essential for this task to avoid spending time trying to avoid standing on top of each other. | Try to use the first two set of tiles surrounding the centre piece, with one player following another. | In hard mode, chunks of flesh will fall from the ceiling for the entire fight, so players should be mindful of this to avoid taking unnecessary damage and stuns, which can potentially allow the Bloat to damage them. | If the bloat manages to attack someone, use Protect from Missiles to reduce damage, since everyone is likely to be hit. | When the bloat is inactive, be mindful to avoid death-dotting on each other, as this will disqualify the team if this occurs. | The team cannot enter after the first stomp(?), as it will fail the task saying "Player A has entered the room late."

column6: In the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode, complete the Nylocas room without ever letting the Nylocas Prinkipas change styles.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Nylocas;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode;Nylocas Prinkipas
column10: Nylocas Prinkipas has 300/350/400 health (in <3, 4 and 5-man sizes) and like Nylocas Vasilias, will always spawn in its melee form. | It functions much like Vasilias and will change combat styles after 10 ticks (6 seconds), so the team must focus it as soon as it appears in order to complete the achievement. | The required amount of damage per player on average decreases with team size, so attempting this achievement in a 5-man encounter should increase the chances of killing the Prinkipas before they can change combat styles. | This should be done with dragon claws or a crystal halberd special as these deal the most amount of damage. | Players on the Arceuus spellbook can use Death Charge (ideally the upgraded variant) to get a lot of special energy without stalling waves. | A surge potion is also helpful in restoring special attack.

column6: Defeat Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode without anyone sharing the ball with anyone, without anyone dying, and without anyone taking damage from any of its other attacks or stepping on the wrong tile in the maze.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Sotetseg;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode
column10: Pray according to Sotetseg's attacks and keep Protect from Melee on until a projectile requires the player to swap prayers. | This achievement basically mirrors Perfect Sotetseg in normal mode, with the addition of needing to tick eat the large balls. | Players targeted by the large balls must tick eat them as sharing them will disqualify the team from the achievement. | It is possible to dodge the damage from these balls if the team manages to phase Sotetseg before they can damage them. | The maze works similarly as in normal mode, but it will be divided among the players sent into the realm; this shouldn't be a problem for anyone however with proper coordination.

column6: Defeat Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode after letting the exhumeds heal him to full health and without anyone in the team taking any damage.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Xarpus;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode;exhumed
column10: Harder Mode II is essentially the same as following Perfect Xarpus in normal mode, apart from having much less space to move around in general. | As with normal mode, landing dragon warhammer and bandos godsword hits are essential for this task, which is fortunately easier in hard mode as Xarpus' Defence drops to 200 from 250. | Once Xarpus starts the screeching phase, the achievement can be easily completed.

column6: Defeat Verzik Vitur's in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode without anyone in your team causing a Nylocas to explode by getting too close.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Verzik Vitur;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode;nylocas
column10: Nylocas will spawn in phase 2 and 3 of the fight. | Up to three nylocas may spawn, consisting of a mix of Nylocas Hagios, Nylocas Ischyros or Nylocas Toxobolos. | The nylocas change styles in hard mode, looping from melee, ranged, and magic every 3 ticks, always in that order. | The nylocas will pursue a random player upon spawning, though it is possible for them to focus on one player instead. | Use the respective weapon against each nylocas to kill them. | Binding the nylocas can make it easier for players to take them down without needing to run a lot. | An effective strategy is to equip an Eye of Ayak and be prepared to attack ranged nylocas as soon as they change. | Without any additional magic damage bonus, this will always kill the nylocas in one hit as long as your current Magic level is at least 93. | In phase 2, these are always accompanied by a Nylocas Athanatos. | It is recommended to keep the Athanatos alive, as its presence will prevent any additional nylocas from spawning until 35.0% or less health, where two Nylocas Matomenos begin to periodically spawn. | The healing that the Athanatos provides can generally be outpaced by the team. | In phase 3, they appear as Verzik's first special attack (after 4 auto attacks), and will not be used until 16 auto-attacks later when she loops her special attack rotation again. | These should be killed off as soon as they spawn. | Even though it's not specifically stated, you cannot die yourself during this task. | If you die during Verzik the task will not complete for you, but it will for the rest of the team.

column6: When Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode uses her yellow power blast attack while the tornadoes are active, have everyone get through the attack without taking damage. This cannot be completed with one player alive
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Verzik Vitur;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode

column6: Defeat Verzik Vitur in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode without anyone attacking her with a melee weapon during her third phase.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Verzik Vitur;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode
column10: The player has the option to choose between the staff of the dead (as it is considered a magic weapon), a twisted bow or Tumeken's shadow for this achievement. | Verzik has a Defence level of 150 along with +30 slash, +100 magic and +230 ranged defence bonuses. | Verzik's magic defence rolls off her Defence level rather than Magic in a manner similar to the ice demon, which can make Tumeken's shadow more consistent and high-hitting. | It is best to avoid brewing whenever possible however, as this will reduce its effectiveness. | As long as the player does not die against Verzik, the achievement will be gained.

column6: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time, with no deaths and without anyone buying anything from a supply chest.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode;Chest (Theatre of Blood)
column10: A stamina potion may be helpful to bring for both the Nylocas room and Verzik's fight. | Only 1-2 players need to bring one with Boost Potion Share if they share the doses before the Nylocas room and/or before Verzik's web attack. | Players should try to only use supplies at the Nylocas and Verzik's fight. | Prayer potions might be needed at the Maiden, Bloat and Sotetseg if necessary, but do not waste too much as the supplies will be needed for Verzik. | Plan on saving at least 3 Saradomin brews and 3 Super restores for Verzik's fight in case of mistakes, meaning you should try to bring at least 4 brews and 4 restores into the raid to be safe. | Avoid extra hits at bloat if they would result in tanking flies or stomps. | Bring an extra brew and hard food for emergencies and to heal before Nylocas Vasilias or during the waves | Time Sotetseg's death ball with his shadow maze attack to remove the need to heal off its damage or camp low hitpoints.

column6: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time.
column10: Completing the raid in the challenge time is easiest in a group of 4 or 5. | Time between the rooms is also counted, so players should avoid spending too much time waiting on teammates and buying supplies.

column10: This combat task is as easy as it sounds. | You just need to enter the arena on the opposite side from where you enter. | You do not need to finish the raid to complete the combat task. | Therefore, if you just leave the raid after entering the arena you can greatly simplify your setup and inventory by just using your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter and not bothering to fight the Pestilent Bloat. | Useful if you just need 4 combat points to achieve the next combat achievement. | However, it is worth attempting to fight the Pestilent Bloat and try to complete the Appropriate Tools and Chally Time combat tasks by bringing some melee gear and a suitable halberd. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.) | Completing these 3 fairly easy tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

column9: Combat Achievements/Elite;Pestilent Bloat;Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode;dragon halberd;crystal halberd;special attack
column10: You do not need to complete the raid to complete the combat task. | Therefore, if you just leave the raid after defeating the Pestilent Bloat you can simplify your inventory as the mage gear switch required for later in the raid will not be required. | Your inventory can thus hold more food and potions to get you through the task. | It is advisable to take your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter, (consider completing the Anticoagulants achievement at this time), then switch to your best melee gear with a suitable halberd to complete this task by killing the Pestilent Bloat with a halberd special attack. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.) | The They Won't Expect This and Appropriate Tools task can also be easily achieved at the same time as this task. | So if you are looking for a few points to get to the next combat achievement unlock, completing these 3 tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

column6: In the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, freeze any 4 Nylocas with a single Ice Barrage spell.
column9: Combat Achievements/Elite;nylocas;Ice Barrage;Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode
column10: The easiest way to complete this achievement is to wait until at least halfway through the Nylocas encounter. | When there are enough Nylocas stacked around a pillar, casting Ice barrage on the group will likely complete the achievement. | During Maiden, in groups of 2 or more, there is a chance that the South 4,5 and North 4,5 Matomenos will all spawn. | They will clump together after a few seconds and can be frozen in unison, easily completing the achievement.

column6: Defeat Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode after having split the big ball with your entire team. This must be done with a group size of at least 2.
Kill Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without him reflecting any damage to anyone.
Survive Verzik Vitur's pillar phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without losing a single pillar.
column9: Combat Achievements/Elite;Verzik Vitur;Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode;Supporting Pillar
column10: Have every player use the Dawnbringer's special attack multiple times to quickly end the encounter. | Avoid teammates spreading between multiple pillars. | If one pillar is taking too much damage, preemptively move to another.

column6: Survive Verzik Vitur's second phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without anyone getting bounced by Verzik.
column9: Combat Achievements/Elite;Verzik Vitur;Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode
column10: If you fail this achievement you can die and re-attempt Verzik within the same raid. | You do not need to fully complete the raid to finish this task; you must simply defeat Verzik's 2nd phase without getting bounced.

column6: In the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, successfully pass on the green ball to a team mate.
column10: The ball must either target the player or be passed from another teammate in order to attempt to pass it to another player. | Once the ball is targeting the player, stand near another player to bounce the ball and complete the achievement. | Right-click following another player is an easy way to stay close to them.

column6: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode in less than 17 minutes.
column10: Entry mode should prove to be no problem for most players; the only issue will be the Nylocas room and it is recommended to run a trio so the room can be cleared without much hassle.

column6: Complete the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode 1 time.
Kill a Hill Giant, Moss Giant and Fire Giant in the Giant Cave within the Shayzien region.
column9: Combat Achievements/Easy;hill giant;moss giant;fire giant;Giants' Den;Shayzien

column6: Deal 100 damage to creatures using undead thralls.
Kill Phosani's Nightmare once.
Kill Phosani's Nightmare 5 times.
Kill Phosani's Nightmare 25 times.

Kill Phosani's Nightmare while only taking damage from husks, power blasts and weakened Parasites. Also, without having your attacks slowed by the Nightmare Spores or letting a Sleepwalker reach Phosani's Nightmare.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Phosani's Nightmare;Husk (Phosani's Nightmare);Parasite (Phosani's Nightmare);Spore;Sleepwalker (Phosani's Nightmare)
column10: The task is fairly achievable as the player should always be aiming to achieve a perfect kill anyway, as any mistakes result in harsh damage dealt. | Mechanically, the largest threat is Spores, as each spore has a 3x3 AoE, meaning the player must be careful while navigating across totems. | Because the task also requires no sleepwalkers to reach the boss, Dreamland Express is mandatory.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare within 7 minutes and 30 seconds.
column10: For strategies on this achievement, see Phosani's Speedrunner.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare within 6 minutes.
column10: Good gear is required for the achievement. | Scythe of Vitur with Inquisitor's armour is recommended, but an Inquisitor's mace or Soulreaper axe with Bandos armour will suffice to make time. | For the totems, full magic switch and a Tumeken's shadow or an Eye of Ayak are also recommended. | Although very unlikely, it is realistically possible over hundreds of kills with an abyssal bludgeon and trident of the swamp as well, although this requires good execution of mechanics, a great deal of luck, and saving time whenever possible (such as eating in between phases). | A Crimson kisten or Voidwaker is helpful for its consistent and high-damage special attacks. | There are some strategies that may be used to save time beyond standard execution and minimising time wasted: | Using a Scythe of Vitur to deal the finishing blow on the last totem of each phase; this causes it to register as charged one tick sooner due to the overkill hitsplat | Using a ham joint on husks and elder maul/godsword (on crush) on the parasites to immediately kill them with minimal ticks wasted | Using a lightbearer to perform additional special attacks in the overall fight, Death Charge on husks, parasites or sleepwalkers and bringing an ultor ring switch | Running to where Phosani's Nightmare will be after her surge attack to resume attacking her immediately | As the boss is located in an instance, players going specifically for this achievement may opt to reset the fight if the start is slow.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare while killing every parasite and husk in one hit.
column10: Both the husk and parasite will take damage equal to the player's maximum hit if a weapon with a crush attack style is used to attack them. | Husks have 20 health and can be instantly killed by most forms of crush-based weaponry, while Parasites have 55 health, which can be dealt with using a strong two-handed weapon like a godsword, elder maul, soulreaper axe or the special attack of the dragon mace. | The unweakened variant gains extra health, which is too high for these weapons. | Note that if a thrall attacks either at the same time the player does, the achievement will fail.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare without allowing your prayer to be disabled.
column10: The prayer disabling mechanic only takes place in phase 3, doing so prior to launching an incoming attack; players need only deactivate their protection prayer right after the attack lands.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare without a sleepwalker reaching her during her desperation phase.
column10: The Nightmare in phase 4 will have 150 health. | Acceptable special attacks include the crimson kisten, Voidwaker, dragon claws, and granite maul (with an ornate maul handle attached) in that order. | The kisten is the most consistent of the four due to taking advantage of the Nightmare's weakness to crush, while the Voidwaker is only slightly worse than it due to the lower damage range despite having a higher max hit and guaranteed accuracy. | The first sleepwalker will spawn as soon as the phase begins, and will reach the Nightmare in ~15 game ticks, damaging the player around ~17-18 ticks. | This will allow for four attacks with a 4-tick weapon such as an Inquisitor's mace, or three with a Scythe of Vitur. | With high-hitting special attacks, the player should be able to subdue the Nightmare before the first sleepwalker even reaches her. | If the sleepwalker ends up reaching the Nightmare, the player is only disqualified if pink petals fall on the player, as this indicates damage was inflicted. | If these petals do not appear as the Nightmare is subdued, the player will not be damaged.

column6: Kill Phosani's Nightmare 5 times in a row without leaving Phosani's Dream.
column10: With a proper Phosani's Nightmare kill, the player's only source of damage should come from sleepwalkers at the end of phases 1-3, parasites when they burst from the player, and any sleepwalkers that reach Phosani's Nightmare during phase 4. | Since the player's inventory will be full of prayer restoration potions, this will leave them with no food to recover from mistakes. | Ideal substitutes to restore health from chip damage and minor mistakes should be done with an amulet of blood fury, Sanguinesti staff, and a Saradomin godsword. | The latter requires special attack energy however, and has to be used on a parasite, sleepwalker or husk to get the most out of it. | Phosani's Nightmare can provide some supplies in the form of Saradomin brews, prayer potions, Sanfew serums, bass, and sharks, which will last for 30 minutes in the instance. | As the player should generally take minimal or no damage from mechanics, prayer potions and Sanfew serums are much more vital for the achievement. | Try to line a kill up with food or potion drops, depending on what is brought more. | Food is more common than potions, so it may be best to start with a full inventory of potions rather than food. | A Scythe of Vitur can generally be seen as a more effective choice than an Inquisitor's mace due to the two extra hits made per attack, though it is less accurate, and players would need to bring a ham joint to kill off the husks. | An ideal kill would generally take around 5-6 minutes (primarily depending overall performance) and consumes around two 4-dose prayer potions (with moderate flicking) and two doses of divine super combat potion. | For five kills, the player should bring three 4-dose divine combat potions and 11 or 12 Sanfew serums. | Depending on the player's speed, they may use anywhere from 0-3 doses of sanfew serum per kill. | Alternatively, players can forgo magic equipment to allow for more inventory spaces for potions and food. | A halberd swap is recommended for this as one of the spore layouts will prevent players from using melee without running into one.

column6: Kill Nex once.
Kill Nex 25 times.
column10: This achievement can be quickly completed by joining the any of the Nex mass worlds.

column6: Kill Nex without anyone dying.
Kill Nex without letting her heal from her Blood Siphon special attack.
column10: Players must not attack Nex after she shouts as any damage done during that period will heal her instead. | Any Blood Reavers that spawn must also be killed before she uses the special attack again.

column6: Kill Nex without anyone taking damage from any Ice special attack.
column10: Players must stay away from melee distance upon her using her Containment attack and quickly free any imprisoned teammates upon her using her Ice Prison attack. | Both Osmumten's fang and Dragon warhammer are particularly accurate against the ice walls, but any crush weapon will work well.

column6: Kill Nex without anyone being hit by the Smoke Dash special attack.
column10: Players can avoid this attack by standing on the outside of the arena before the attack. | If standing in melee distance, Nex will look at the direction she intends to dash towards prior to the attack as a warning indicator to avoid that lane.

column6: Kill Nex with three or less players at the start of the fight.
Kill Nex with two or less players at the start of the fight.
Kill Nex whilst a player is coughing.
column10: For the task to be completed, players must purposely spread the virus to other players for the entirety of the fight. | Players will cough four times (three with a slayer helmet) for each cough, which resets if they infect another player with it. | The best way to complete the achievement is to have two or three players purposely infect each other while the rest of the team takes down Nex. | These players should ideally not engage Nex in battle to avoid spreading the virus to other players who will be killing Nex.

column6: Kill Nex whilst completing the requirements for "There is no escape", "Shadows move", "A siphon will solve this", and "Contain this!"
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Nex;There is no escape!;Shadows Move...;A siphon will solve this;Contain this!

column6: Kill Nex without anyone being hit by the Shadow Smash attack.
Complete the Tombs of Amascut (normal) within 18 mins at any group size.
column10: When attempting to complete the combat achievement, the following are the approximate times which the player should aim for each stage of the raid: | Gear Recommendations, for a duo, include max armour for all 3 combat styles: Torva, Masori, and Ancestral. | Twisted Bow, Dragon Arrows, Blowpipe, Zaryte Crossbow, Tumeken's Shadow, Avernic Defender, Dragon Dagger, Dragon Claws, and one player with Thralls with the other player on the Lunar Spellbook for Vengeance/Vengeance Other. | Both players could also use the Lunar Spellbook and use spellbook swap to use Thralls and Vengeance.

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut (expert) within 20 mins at any group size.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Tombs of Amascut;Tombs Speed Runner III

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut (expert) within 18 mins in a group of 8.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Tombs of Amascut;Group Ironman Mode
column10: All players should ideally have a high Mining level to clear Het's challenge in one cycle to avoid wasting extra time with the 1-tick pre-mining method to get an additional hit in. | All players are required to have near or best-in-slot gear as players must burst through the bosses very quickly. | The bosses will have ~5.78 times the amount of health they would in solo. | As it is important to move fast in between rooms it is also recommended to leave some inventory space, as to not have to drop and pick up items. | With proper play food won't be needed until Wardens, where one should use Ambrosia. | Selecting easy invocations will minimise frustration during the attempt, and it is important that players do not die during the bosses, as even one player dying can significantly set the team back. | The zaryte crossbow with Ruby dragon bolts (e) can deal a lot of damage with its special attack. | One player should bring an elder maul or dragon warhammer, while another brings a soulflame horn to make Ba-Ba and Kephri easier to handle. | A player can bring a Keris partisan of corruption to use its special attack to allow teammates to deal more damage for a short duration. | Another option is for the whole team to camp mage and use Eye of Ayak's special attack at the start of each boss, with the exception of Akkha, who can be zaryte crossbow specced thrice with liquid adrenaline and surge potion. | The baboons in Apmeken's challenge are very straightforward following the changes on 24 May 2024 and 25 June 2025, as players are guaranteed max hits on combat baboons and specialist baboons barely have any health. | Ba-Ba should be dragged as close to the southern end of the arena as possible reduce the amount of time spent falling after her roar. | The baboons should be ignored to send her to the next phase as soon as possible. | The path of Crondis can be sped up by synchronising the collection of the water jugs, bypassing the respawn time on the waterfalls and avoiding any damage to the Palm of Resourcefulness from the crocodiles. | Having a person enter with the "Pass" option instead of "Quick-Pass", whilst the rest of the team spams "Pass", guarantees everyone to be synced up. | Zebak's fight is fairly straightforward. | Minimise time spent pushing water jugs and avoiding waves. | For Kephri, two or three players should act as swarm killers, killing the scarab swarms that appear during the interlude phases to minimise the amount of healing Kephri can recover; if done properly, she will only recover with 1 health, often resulting in the next hit putting her out. | On the 2nd phase, kill the Soldier Scarab as soon as possible to limit healing while keeping the Arcane Scarab from attacking. | At Akkha, one player should serve as a butterfly, kiting Akkha so that he never gets the chance to attack the team. | It is recommended to have Feeling Special active, so the memory blast attack can be performed faster. | Use Tumeken's shadow on him unless he enters his magic stance, after which players should begin using a fang instead. | The Wardens can be completed as normal. | Try to clear the second phase within two core downs, ideally with Tumeken's Warden being fought for the last two phases. | Assuming a normal raid level of 300 with no path levelling, the enemies will have the following health: | Zebak: 7400 | Kephri: 1910 (shield), 1020 (unguarded) | Akkha: 5100 | Ba-Ba: 4850 | Obelisk: 3320 | Wardens: 1790 (shield), 33930 (core), 11230 (phase 3) | Skulls: 4

column6: Complete a full Tombs of Amascut raid only using supplies given inside the tomb and without anyone dying.
column10: Players should pre-pot (including with an extended anti-venom+) before entering the raid. | Using a Falador shield to restore prayer and the Keris partisan of the sun special attack or Blood Spells to restore health will not fail the task. | Health, prayer, run energy and special attack are also restored after clearing each path. | It is recommended to prioritise taking nectar and tears of Elidinis from the Helpful Spirit. | Ambrosia is also useful as it is the only way to cure poison or venom. | Start with Zebak and Kephri first since they can be cleared with little damage taken, then take care to avoid the Cursed Baboon's venom trails in the Path of Apmeken.

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut without using any supplies from the Helpful Spirit and without anyone dying. Honey locusts are included in this restriction.
column10: Bring a 4-dose potion of super combat and ranging. | For a magic boost, bring an imbued or saturated heart instead. | Ancient and forgotten brews can be used in place of the heart, but this will drain melee stats in the process. | As the player will not have access to smelling salts and liquid adrenaline, be prepared to three cycle the Warden on phase 2. | Other than that, the bosses can be killed fairly easily on a raid level of 150 with good gear.

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut with the "On a diet" and "Dehydration" invocations activated and without anyone dying.
column10: To complete this task, it is highly recommended that the player has an amulet of blood fury and Keris partisan of the sun. | A Sanguinesti staff is helpful, but not absolutely required if the player possesses Tumeken's shadow. | On a Diet prevents players from using solids (e.g sharks) and also prevents the Helpful Spirit from giving Silk dressings. | Dehydration prevents players from using potions to heal (e.g Saradomin brews), which also means that players cannot use nectar or ambrosia either. | The only bosses where players may take significant damage would be Wardens and Akkha, as Zebak, Kephri and Ba-Ba should not deal any significant damage at all due to their attacks being easily avoidable and/or blocked. | The player's main source of healing will be from the sun keris, as its passive restores 12 health and overheals to 20% of their base Hitpoints level at the cost of 5 prayer points. | This effect is particularly useful at the Wardens' phase 3 to heal off the skulls during the interludes. | In addition, it has a special attack that fully restores health and overheals 20% of their Hitpoints level at the cost of 50 prayer points, which can be very useful in a pinch. | The Saradomin Godsword and toxic blowpipe are also a viable option for providing healing power through the Wardens fight. | Since "Dehydration" and "On a Diet" are active, the player should only select the "Power" option from the Helpful Spirit, which provides both a smelling salt and liquid adrenaline. | The "Chaos" option is only useful if the pack contains adrenaline and tears of Elidinis, although this scenario is usually unlikely and thus players can simply choose another power option instead. | Due to the extra adrenaline, players can dump special attacks on whoever is the last boss to slightly speed up the kill time.

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut without anyone in your party wearing or holding any equipment at tier 75 or above.
column10: As tier 75 or higher equipment cannot be used, players will be unable to use most reasonable weapons and equipment that would make the raid faster. | The second-best alternatives to use in lieu of them would be the gear setup below. | If crystal armour is outside of your ability/price, hunters' sunlight crossbow, an odium ward and moonlight antler bolts are good alternatives to the crystal bow as the high attack speed can compensate for some of the accuracy and strength loss. | Thralls are allowed. | Burning Claws and Belle's Folly are eligible and can be brought in as a spec weapon and stab weapon respectively. | Unlike the tier 65 Keris partisan, the Keris partisan of the sun, Keris partisan of breaching, Keris partisan of amascut and Keris partisan of corruption cannot be brought into the raid as they require 80 Attack. | Below is an example equipment and inventory that can be used to complete this task. | Quantities and ratios of supplies needed is very dependant on how experienced a player is with the Tombs of Amascut raid. | Example inventory might not apply to everyone, and players should make adjustments based on their own skills. | Despite being equipment that is tier 75 or higher, the following items may currently be used without failing the task: | Holy ghrazi rapier | Holy sanguinesti staff | Holy and Sanguine Scythe of Vitur | Ancient sceptre with quartz attached | Desert treasure 2 rings | Max cape variants of Dizana's quiver | Amulet of rancour (s) | Echo Virtus robes | Lastly, dying does not disqualify the player for the task; as long as one teammate survives and completes the raid, the task is completed for all participants.

column6: Defeat Zebak using only melee attacks and without dying yourself.
column10: At the minimum raid level of 150, Zebak will have 930 health. | Zebak's melee attack hits the hardest and can also apply a bleeding effect that deals additional damage if the player moves. | Assuming no path levelling is active (which should most likely be the case), Zebak will have an attack speed of 7, or once every 4.2 seconds. | Once he enrages, his attack speed increases to 4, or every 2.4 seconds. | Use the best melee weapons and armour you have access to, prioritising melee accuracy and strength bonuses over defensive bonuses. | Defence reducing special attacks, such as the Bandos godsword's, can be used since like Ba-Ba he does not reset his Defence level. | However, his Defence can only be lowered to 50 (from 70 and before modifications). | He has fairly high defensive bonuses (+160 stab, slash and +260 crush), so Osmumten's fang is highly effective due to its passive effect. | All melee damage from Zebak can be avoided by using a flinching method. | This is done by attacking Zebak from three tiles away, and immediately after, running out of his melee attack range. | Zebak's melee attack has a one tick delay, so if the player only stays in his melee range for one tick at a time, his melee attacks will never damage the player. | Alternative, easier but slower, strategy is to use a crystal halberd or noxious halberd to attack him standing two tiles away causing him to never use his melee attack. | Note: Usage of ghostly and skeletal thralls, recoil damage (e.g. ring of recoil, Vengeance), and the Voidwaker's special attack will all fail the challenge. | However, both zombie thralls and burn damage from Burning claws's special attack will not fail the challenge, and ranged weapons can be used to break the jugs.

column6: Complete phase three of The Wardens in a group of two or more, using only melee attacks and without dying yourself. The 'Insanity' invocation must be activated.
column10: Insanity can only be toggled on when both "Overclocked" and "Overclocked 2" are active, which when combined with "Insanity" will make the Warden attack every 3 ticks. | The Warden will have 1940 health per player at a raid level of 300, resulting in it having a total of 1940* party size health. | Each slam attack will deal roughly 40-50 damage if not avoided. | The player must move immediately after attacking to avoid getting hit by the slam, as there is no time to dodge the attack when within five tiles from the boss. | The boss will also have four interlude phases entwined at 20% health intervals which release more Energy Siphons in a different layout compared to solo, however despite having "Insanity" there is still a larger amount of time to reverse the skulls before they explode. | It is possible to survive with 80+ health with one skull untouched, but two or more result in instant death unless the player somehow manages to avoid the resulting explosion. | Supply invocations should be left untouched, and this should leave players with a significant amount of supplies entering the Wardens. | When the Warden reaches critical health, it will restore 20% of its health and any drained Defence levels and increase its Defence. | This will also cause one of the two phantom bosses (Ba-Ba's Phantom for Tumeken and Akkha's Phantom for Elidinis) to attack faster. | Players should use Osmumten's fang for the task, as it is the most accurate of melee weapons due to the passive effect it has while in the raid, despite the Warden's slightly higher stab resistance. | To handle defence drains, one player should use a soulflame horn while the other uses a dragon warhammer or elder maul special attack, as this will reduce its Defence to the maximum; 30 drained levels pre-enrage and 60 post-enrage, significantly increasing accuracy. | Warning: While thralls can be used for this achievement, they must be zombified thralls; using ghostly or Skeletal thralls will cause disqualification. | Overclocked must be active in order to activate this invocation. | The slam attack is performed 3 ticks faster. | There is less time to reverse the Energy Siphons. | The slam attack resumes based on where the Warden left off prior to launching Energy Siphons rather than resetting positions. | Red lightning strikes faster. | Each row of floor tiles is removed at a faster pace. | Overclocked 2 must be active in order to activate this invocation.

column6: Complete the Tombs of Amascut in a group of two or more without anyone dying.
Complete the Tombs of Amascut solo without dying.
Complete the Het room without taking any damage from the light beam and orbs. You must destroy the core after one exposure.
column9: File:Path of Het puzzle.png;Combat Achievements/Elite;Path of Het;Orb of Darkness;Het's Seal
column10: Level 85 Mining (boostable from 82 with a Dragon pickaxe) is required for this task in a solo encounter in order to deal enough damage to Het's Seal in one cycle. | There is more leeway in group encounters depending on the Mining level of the other teammates and if they are one-tick clicking the pillar before the beam hits the shielded statue, as this provides an extra hit to the statue before the next cycle starts (see Tombs of Amascut/Strategies for the one-cycle method). | The team should take time setting down mirrors to ensure that the beam won't hit them as they set it and watch out for any orbs that appear while setting the mirrors and mining the pillar, as they have a notorious habit of forcing players to move out of the way when the pillar is being destroyed. | A boosted Mining level of 100 or higher will allow destroying the core without the one-tick prep in a solo encounter.

column6: Complete Akkha in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Akkha's attacks off-prayer, Akkha's special attacks (orbs, memory, detonate), exploding shadow timers, orbs in the enrage phase or attacking Akkha with the wrong style. You must have all Akkha invocations activated.
column10: Using a melee thrall in the final phase of the fight will fail this combat achievement. | It is not known whether this is intended or a bug. | However, as Akkha has a chance to change his combat style with every special, it is not recommended to use thralls when attempting this achievement, even if the player starting the encounter is confident with their "butterfly" technique. | As Double Trouble needs to be activated with multiple players, the player butterflying Akkha should dodge the memory attack in the middle, while other players should use the "staircase" technique to skip the memory attack at the edges of the arena. | If Akkha switches styles and uses black orbs at the same time, it may be safer to stay still and flick protection prayers, rather than attempting to flinch. | Since the achievement is under Tombs of Amascut, the fastest method is to attempt the achievement with a raid level of 150 with all Akkha invocations active, reducing his health.

column6: Complete 'Perfect Het' and 'Perfect Akkha' in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Perfect Het;Perfect Akkha;Tombs of Amascut
column10: Perfect Het and Perfect Akkha do not need to be completed in succession. | As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Het and then fail Perfect Akkha can all die and re-attempt Perfect Akkha without having to redo Perfect Het.

column6: Complete the Apmeken room in a group of two or more, without anyone allowing any dangers to trigger, standing in venom or being hit by a volatile baboon. You must complete this room in less than three minutes.
column10: Hammers and Neutralising potion are provided in crates in the room before the challenge can start. | When the first player enters the challenge area, they will obtain Apmeken's Sight, which allows them to identify dangers and resolve them before they damage the team. | If the pillars have an issue, call out P; if the vents have an issue, call V. | If corruption is spreading, death-dot (in larger groups) or use the potion on the corrupted player (smaller groups). | Freeze any Cursed Baboons and immediately kill them to avoid spreading venom. | Volatile Baboons can be easily avoided as their explosion is a 3x3 AoE centered around them; they can also be killed, but it is not required. | Following the 29 May 2024 update to the Path of Apmeken, this achievement is significantly easier as the baboons have very little health and can be easily killed in one or a few hits.

column6: Defeat Ba-Ba in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Ba-Ba's Attacks off-prayer, Ba-Ba's slam, rolling boulders, rubble attack or falling rocks. No sarcophagi may be opened. You must have all Ba-Ba invocations activated.
Complete 'Perfect Apmeken' and 'Perfect Ba-Ba' in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Perfect Apmeken;Perfect Ba-Ba;Tombs of Amascut
column10: The Path of Apmeken does not need to be completed in 3 minutes, as is normally required for Perfect Apmeken. | Additionally, it and Perfect Ba-Ba do not need to be completed in succession. | As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Apmeken and then fail Perfect Ba-Ba can all die and re-attempt Perfect Ba-Ba without having to redo Perfect Apmeken.

column6: Complete the Crondis room without letting a crocodile get to the tree, without anyone losing water from their container and in under one minute.
column9: Combat Achievements/Elite;Path of Crondis;crocodile (Tombs of Amascut);Palm of Resourcefulness;water container (Tombs of Amascut)
column10: Since deaths restart this task, one (except hardcore iron men) may save a few ticks by entering the puzzle room just to get the water container, then dying to restart the task, as it will appear in the inventory after death. | Also, in case one fails, a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake may be used to reset the task faster.

column6: Defeat Zebak without anyone taking any damage from: poison, Zebak's basic attacks off-prayer, blood spawns and waves. You also must not push more than two jugs on the roar attack during the fight (you may destroy stationary ones). You must have all Zebak invocations activated.
column10: As Upset Stomach will be active, remember to take note that the water jugs have a 3x3 AoE and acid pools 5x5. | Taking damage from Zebak's roar attack will not cause the achievement to fail, so it can be significantly easier to tank the roar attack each time it happens and focus on dealing damage instead of setting up the jugs. | Make sure the tile in front of you and a few tiles behind you are clear to not get pushed into acid during the attack. | If one is specifically going for this achievement and healing is a concern for tanking, one can simply disable any of the lives invocations and die repeatedly to Zebak with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake to obtain enough Honey locusts, which are stackable and can overheal above max health. | Simply leave the raid after successfully completing the achievement. | With sufficient DPS, it's possible to skip one of the four special attacks Zebak would use, minimising the chances of failing the achievement as the acid pools are the only concern for the task. | Standing next to the ramp to the water should avoid most if not all of the acid pools. | It is important to note that getting hit by the water jugs does not fail the achievement attempt. | Zebak will occasionally cast a form of Blood Blitz on all players. | This attack will always hit regardless of defensive bonuses, unless Protect from Magic is active; if damage is inflicted, Zebak will slightly heal. | Getting hit by this without Protect from Magic active will not fail the achievement. | He will also summon Blood Clouds that rapidly sap the player's health if next to one. | Not Just a Head must be active in order to activate this invocation. | Not Just a Head must be active in order to activate this invocation.

column6: Complete 'Perfect Crondis' and 'Perfect Zebak' in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Perfect Crondis;Perfect Zebak;Tombs of Amascut

column6: Complete the Scabaras room in less than a minute without anyone taking any damage from puzzles.
column10: The achievement is best done in a solo encounter while avoiding the pillars room, since this room is a guessing game and can take a while to solve. | The last puzzle is incapable of damaging players. | A fast way to reattempt the combat achievement is to log out of the raid and start a new raid.

column6: Defeat Kephri in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: egg explosions, Kephri's attacks, Exploding Scarabs, Bodyguards, dung attacks. No eggs may hatch throughout the fight.
Complete 'Perfect Scabaras' and 'Perfect Kephri' in a single run of Tombs of Amascut.
column9: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster;Perfect Scabaras;Perfect Kephri;Tombs of Amascut
